OVERRIDE OF THE QUESTIONNAIRE (identidad options): the printed P.10 [IDENTIDAD] response list in cues3480.pdf (page 5, confirmed in the rendered page image as well as the text layer) shows only four substantive options -- 'Únicamente español/a ....1', 'Más español/a que (gentilicio de su Comunidad Autónoma) ....2', 'Tan español/a como (gentilicio de su Comunidad Autónoma) ....4', 'Únicamente (gentilicio de su Comunidad Autónoma) ....5' -- i.e. it omits 'Más (gentilicio) que español/a' and numbers 'Tan ... como' as 4. The .sav and ES3480 value labels list all five: 1 'Únicamente español/a', 2 'Más español/a que (gentilicio de C.A.)', 3 'Tan español/a como (gentilicio de C.A.)', 4 'Más (gentilicio de C.A.) que español/a', 5 'Únicamente (gentilicio de C.A.)'. The data follow the value labels: code 3 is the plurality (1978 of 3687, the usual 'as Spanish as regional' modal answer) and code 4 is populated (502), neither possible under the printed list. Ordering check: mean p9 (1 = single central government ... 5 = right to independence) by identidad code is 2.2/2.4/2.8/3.7/4.6 for codes 1..5 (r = 0.45, n = 3631), monotone as the value-label order requires with code 4 sitting between 'as Spanish as' and 'only regional'; identidad means are highest in País Vasco 3.4 and Cataluña 3.3 and lowest in Melilla 1.9 and Ceuta/Castilla-La Mancha 2.2. So the questionnaire's IDENTIDAD list is a printing defect (a dropped line plus renumbering) and the shipped option_text follows the value labels. TEXT (text_source=study_materials): P.9 and P.10 are two separate questions, each with its own response set, so instructions is blank and each full question is its item_text (spain_2023_identity_state/europe shape); single trivial section_id. Each item_text is the full question text from cues3480.pdf verbatim including the interviewer direction printed with it (batch_583-589 convention), only the 'P.9'/'P.10' numbering dropped, line breaks joined with a space; asserted present verbatim in the whitespace-collapsed pdftotext -raw layer (build.R). OPTIONS = the .sav/ES3480 value labels verbatim for both items (asserted in build.R). For p9 the five printed questionnaire options agree character for character with the value labels (option 1 carries a trailing period in the questionnaire only; label form shipped, as in spain_2023_identity_state). For identidad the value labels are the only source listing all five options (see OVERRIDE); they abbreviate the CATI demonym fill as '(gentilicio de C.A.)' where the questionnaire prints '(gentilicio de su Comunidad Autónoma)' -- respondents heard their own region's demonym; the label placeholder is shipped rather than mixing the two forms. identidad 7 '(NO LEER) Ninguna de las anteriores', 8 N.S., 9 N.C. and p9 8 N.S., 9 N.C. are set to missing by the .do and get no rows. Every item has an option row for all five levels, and all five are used on both items. STEP 3b: dictionary Description ('Preferred territorial organization of the Spanish state and strength of regional versus Spanish national identity') matches P.9 + P.10; 2 items, resp 1..5; no instrument mismatch. public_note: The printed CIS questionnaire lists only four identity options (it omits 'more [regional] than Spanish' and numbers 'as Spanish as [regional]' 4), but the data and the file's value labels use five codes, 1 only Spanish ... 5 only [regional], and the option text follows the value labels; '[regional]' stands for the demonym of the respondent's own autonomous community; 'none of the above', don't-know and no-answer are stored as missing; English is IRW machine translation of the Spanish-only CIS questionnaire
